messages:
SupportBot: heads up — multiple customers (S-42, S-91, S-114) reporting sudden p99 latency jump on /v1/generate since ~03:00 UTC. Backend traces show long queue_wait and lots of requests stuck in 'admit' state. No obvious model change in prod on the surface.

Priya: ok grabbing logs + traces. are these all in hosted-prod region us-west-2? any correlation with dedicated customers?

SupportBot: yes, primarily us-west-2 hosted. Dedicated customers unaffected so far. Appears to be surge on small models (alpaca-7b-quant).

Alex: checking admission-control metrics now — can you paste the trace ids?

SupportBot: trace ids: 3f2a8b, 3f2a8c, 3f2b1a. sample log snippet:```
[2026-03-15T03:12:07Z] request_id=3f2a8b queue_wait=612ms worker_acquire_wait=0ms service=admit reason=batcher-throttle
[2026-03-15T03:12:07Z] request_id=3f2a8b model=alpaca-7b-quant status=queued queue_index=237
[2026-03-15T03:12:08Z] request_id=3f2a8b result=timeout error=admit_timeout
```

Jorge: looks like the batcher is forming huge queues and the admit policy is timing out. can we check per-worker inflight counts? maybe a worker got stuck in a hot loop or OOMing and reduced capacity.

Alex: `metrics.admit.enqueue_rate` and `metrics.worker.inflight` show a spike around 03:05. inflight per pod dropped from ~48 -> 6 for several pods. k8s events show repeated pod restarts at that window.

Priya: any recent kernel or docker image changes? DeployBot, did we roll anything around 02:50-03:10?

DeployBot: rollout completed: service/runtime-proxy @ commit 8f7a2d (2026-03-15T02:58:12Z) — canary -> prod. No further rollouts recorded.

Jorge: that commit touched batcher concurrency code? I remember 8f7a2d adjusted the default worker eviction timer.

Alex: yep — 8f7a2d changed the gc loop interval and lowered the per-worker max_inflight to 64 -> 32 in the canary config. It should be safe but maybe combined with a traffic pattern changed worker memory usage and triggered restarts.

Priya: mitigation proposal: 1) temporarily increase max_inflight to previous safe value (64) via runtime feature flag, 2) scale up worker pool by +20% in us-west-2, 3) enable fallback routing to larger model variant (alpaca-7b-quant-fast) for new requests to reduce queueing. who can push the flag?

Alex: I can flip the feature flag for us-west-2 now. command: ```redis-cli -h config-cache.runtime "HSET feature:admit:us-west-2 max_inflight 64"``` will apply immediately to the admission controller. then we should trigger a rolling restart of the runtime-proxy pods to pick up any cached config.

Jorge: scaling up workers: `kubectl scale deployment worker --replicas=24 -n runtime-us-west-2` (current 20 -> 24). I'll do that. also enable fallback routing rule: add route entry so requests to alpaca-7b-quant can fall back to alpaca-7b-quant-fast if queue_wait > 300ms. patch snippet:```yaml
routes:
  - match: model == "alpaca-7b-quant"
    fallback: "alpaca-7b-quant-fast"
    fallback_threshold_ms: 300
```

SupportBot: customers S-42 and S-91 reporting partial recovery after initial mitigation — p99 reduced from ~1.2s -> ~420ms but some residual p95 tail left.

Priya: tracking: root cause seems to be interplay of the new low max_inflight + memory pressure caused by a micro-regression in the batcher GC -> pod restarts -> lower capacity -> long queues. action items: revert the max_inflight change if mitigation holds, run a small canary rollback of 8f7a2d to validate.

Alex: I've set the feature flag and initiated runtime-proxy rolling restart. Monitoring for 10m.

Jorge: workers scaled. I also evicted 2 pods that were repeatedly restarting and collected heap dumps for postmortem. saved to GCS: gs://redwood-debug/heapdumps/2060012345/

DeployBot: rollback triggered for canary: runtime-batcher @ commit 8f7a2d -> 6c4b911 (2026-03-15T03:22:40Z).

Priya: good. once rollback finishes let's re-evaluate for 20m then close the incident if stable. please paste any quick repro steps so support can follow up with customers.

Alex: repro steps for internal QA:
1) run a steady stream of small-model requests to /v1/generate at rps ~180 for 10m with short prompts.
2) concurrently run a few large-context memory-heavy requests to create intermittent GC pressure.
3) observe worker restarts and queue_wait spikes in `metrics.admit.queue_wait` and `kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total`.

SupportBot: will relay repro steps to customers and ask for logs if they still see tails. Thanks all — tracking in incident tracker: INC-206001 (link: https://redwood.internal/incidents/INC-206001). :thumbsup:

Jorge: postmortem notes to follow — looks like we need a test harness for combined small/big request churn. also add an alert: if pod restarts >3 in 15m AND p99 > 500ms trigger paging.

Priya: capturing action items: 1) revert 8f7a2d in prod if rollback not automatic 2) add roll-forward test for batcher GC under mixed workload 3) tighten restart alerting 4) document fallback routing config and quick patch steps.

SupportBot: customers notified with status. I'll update thread if any customer re-open.

Alex: monitoring green at 03:46 UTC. p99 back to baseline (~180ms). I'll leave the flag at 64 for 1h then evaluate.

SupportBot: closing live escalation for now, will keep incident open for postmortem.
